North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 29 at 5:29PM CDT until August 30 at 9:10AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Illinois...
Indiana...

Wabash River at Hutsonville to Vincennes

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Considerable agricultural flooding extends
from just north of the junction of Illinois 33 with Business 50 to
the St. Francesville, Illinois area.  River Road from Lincoln
Memorial Bridge to Billett Rd is impassable.  Extensive seep water
forms behind Illinois levees extending from Russellville to U.S.
Highway 50.  Flooding of agricultural land begins in Knox County
Indiana west of the railroad extending for the Oaktown area to the
north side of Vincennes.  Extensive flooding of Small Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday the stage was 16.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday was 17.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 4.4 feet Tuesday, September
08.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 915 AM CDT /1015
AM EDT/.

properties.description:
At 645 PM MST, Heavy rain has ended. Earlier in the afternoon radar
estimated that from 0.25 to 0.75 inches fell over the area in less
than 30 minutes. As a result, flash flooding along Bright Angel Creek
in the area of Phantom Ranch and the Transept was observed. Heavy
creek flow is ongoing. An air evacuation was conducted of
approximately 50 individuals from the Phantom Ranch area. Kaibab
Trail and Phantom Ranch are closed until further notice.

HAZARD...Flash flooding in and around the Bright Angel Creek Basin
below the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of areas in and around the Bright Angel Creek
Basin below the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bright Angel Point, Phantom Ranch, Pipe Creek Resthouse, Point
Sublime, Cape Royal Point, Grand Canyon National Park, Buddha
Cloister and Vista Encantada.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 87 and 89...and
between river miles 99 and 100.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Ribbon Falls, Bright Angel Campground, North Rim Campground,
Cottonwood Campground, Clear Creek Camp Site, Upper Cremation Camp
Site, Lower Cremation Camp Site, Roy's Beach Camp Site, Boat Beach
Camp Site, Crystal Camp Site, Ego Beach Camp Site, Above Tuna Creek
Camp Site, Above Tuna Rapids Camp Site, Manzanita Rest Area and
Roaring Springs.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Nankoweap Canyon, Crystal Creek, Lava Canyon, Tuna Creek, Unkar
Creek, Slate Creek, Colorado River, Zoroaster Canyon, Clear Creek,
Kwagunt Creek, South Canyon, Shinumo Creek, North Canyon and Bright
Angel Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flash flooding is occurring or imminent downstream of the Dragon
Bravo Fire scar. Severe debris flow are expected downstream of the
North Rim into Bright Angel Creek and Crystal Creek. Campers and
hikers should get away from creeks and move to higher ground
immediately! Stay away or be swept away!
